results.blind_notes: P3: 'Some studies found that larger assortments reduced choosing; others found that they increased it; many found no difference at all.' Opposite effects averaging to near zero = C. B contradicted ('Some studies found ... reduced'); A and D unsupported (P4: 'did not mean that the original study was wrong'). Factually consistent with the Scheibehenne et al. (2010) meta-analysis of ~50 experiments, mean effect ~0.

author_checklist.hardness: Students must distinguish an average effect near zero from no effect in any study; choice B is a strong trap.

results.reason: key, independent computation and blind solve agree; no blocking flags

results.blind_notes: P4: 'This did not mean that the original study was wrong. Rather, it suggested that choice overload depends on circumstances' then lists conditions. Reconciles P3's mixed results with P1's finding. C contradicted; B is P1 content; D is P2 content.

results.blind_notes: P4 conditions: 'no clear preference', 'options are hard to compare', 'must decide quickly'; 'A person who already knows she wants strawberry jam ... is unlikely to be troubled.' B has a clear preference. A = hard to compare; C = must decide quickly + unfamiliar; D = no preference. Well-built application item.

author_checklist.hardness: Students must apply three conditions to four new cases; the key requires recognizing the absence of all three.
